description: Figure 9 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the effect of context masking perturbations on probing accuracy, categorized by grammatical tag: “case,” “gender,” “tag,” “number,” and “tense.” The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” is scaled linearly from 0 to 20, representing the percentage change in probing accuracy (as defined by Equation 1), where positive values indicate a decrease in accuracy and negative values indicate an improvement. The horizontal axis lists the five grammatical tags. For each tag, five bars are grouped together, each corresponding to a different model: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The bars are not sorted; they appear in the order of the models as listed in the legend. The chart shows that the “case” tag exhibits the largest effect magnitudes, with the mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ models showing the highest positive effects (approximately 12 and 11, respectively), while the “tense” tag shows the smallest effects, with all models having values near zero. Error bars, which indicate the standard deviation, are present for each bar, extending above and below the bar’s center.
